name: United Kingdom
official: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

facts.religion: Christian about 46%, no religion about 37%, Muslim about 7%

snapshot: Keir Starmer resigned in June 2026 after a local election rout, and Labour handed the keys to Andy Burnham, Britain's seventh prime minister in ten years.
culture: Britain's cultural reach is vast: Shakespeare, the Beatles, the BBC, the Premier League and Harry Potter. The monarchy, now led by Charles III, remains popular. England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland each have distinct identities, languages and sports traditions, and London is one of the world's most diverse cities.
society: Since leaving the EU in 2020, the UK has struggled with low growth, stagnant wages and strained public services, especially the NHS. Immigration and small boat crossings are central political issues and fuelled Reform UK's rise. Scotland and Wales have devolved governments, and Northern Ireland's power-sharing is fragile.
situation: In 2016, Britain voted to leave the European Union, and it has been looking for a stable leader ever since. Keir Starmer won a landslide in July 2024 promising to end the chaos. Two years later he was gone, and Britain has now had seven prime ministers in a decade, more than at any time since the early 20th century.

The collapse was fast. In May's local elections Labour lost more than 1,000 council seats as Nigel Farage's Reform UK surged, and some polls began predicting Farage as the next prime minister (NPR via Michigan Public). Labour MPs turned on Starmer but had no successor in Parliament. So they made one: a Labour MP stood down, letting Andy Burnham, the popular mayor of Greater Manchester, win a by-election in Makerfield on 18 June. Starmer resigned as party leader on 22 June. Burnham was the only candidate, nominated by 379 of Labour's 403 MPs, and became prime minister on 20 July, promising "to bring back hope" and tackle falling living standards; he calls himself a socialist (ABC News). He ran for the Labour leadership twice before and lost; this time he got it without a contest. One political analyst called him Labour's "last throw of the dice" before an election due by 2029.
power: A parliamentary democracy and constitutional monarchy with no written constitution. The prime minister leads the party with a majority in the 650-seat House of Commons and can change without a general election, as in July. Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland have devolved governments.
holders: Prime Minister Andy Burnham (Labour), since 20 July 2026; King Charles III.
